observations.summary: _archetype_accuracy scores pooled_common (source_backtest.py:527, flattened player-YEARS) with NO per-player dedup, while _xfv_vs_consensus_detail (line 359) DOES dedup 'to ONE row per player: the LATEST pre-debut read'. The archetype AUC therefore counts a stable player once per base year (intl_bat ~2.4x inflated), so a close head-to-head cell can flip sign vs the leakage-clean per-player read. This is the 'intl_bat AUC weak cell' that seeds the experiment queue (weak_cells).
observations.impact: descriptive only (no gate, no served number); can misdirect the queue

observations.proposed_fix: dedup pooled_common to latest pre-debut per player before _archetype_accuracy (mirror _xfv_vs_consensus_detail); or disclose n_unique

observations.summary: the live joint top-band fairness fix reads the SIBLING side's LIVE scored artifact (scored_live_path(other)); regen order is hit-before-pit, so the hit run consumes the PRIOR cycle's pit live board (1-cycle stale) while the pit run consumes the fresh hit board. On a COLD build (no prior sibling artifact) the hit side no-ops entirely while pit applies the fix (verified: forcing the sibling file absent logs 'inputs unavailable -- per-side map kept').
observations.impact: bounded by SFF_MOVE_CAP_FV=3.0 and self-correcting across regens; documented in the docstring. Not a served defect, but an asymmetry worth a cold-build guard.
observations.repro: run_live('hit') with scored_live_path('pit') absent -> _apply_side_fairness_fix returns 0 (no-op); run_live('pit') then applies the joint fix reading fresh hit
observations.proposed_fix: optional: on a missing sibling LIVE artifact, fall back to the sibling RESOLVED pool for the joint band so a cold build is symmetric
